newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK regulators order new IPO allocation measures.
newsitem.headline: HK regulators order new IPO allocation measures.

text.p: Hong Kong's securities regulators and stock exchange said in a joint statement on Thursday they were requiring underwriters to adopt interim allocation procedures for initial public offerings (IPOs).
The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said they had noted that a number of recent IPOs had been significantly oversubscribed.
The present allocation procedure may encourage applicants to apply for large amounts of stock, increasing the demand for funds in the banking system and driving up short term interest rates.

"The SFC and the Exchange are concerned about the potential adverse impact on the securities market of Hong Kong (and) are conducting a study on offer mechanism, which, among other things, will consider means to improve the allocation system in IPOs.

"In order to ensure that the issuance and marketing of securities is conducted in a fair and orderly manner and to maintain investor confidence in the market, the SFC and the Exchange have decided to introduce interim measures to address the effects of the current phenomenon," they said in a statement.
Underwriters would be required to divide the total number of securities available for public subscription equally into two pools, the statement said.

Pool A should be allocated on an equitable basis to applicants who applied for securities in the value of HK$5 million or less, while pool B should be allocated on an equitable basis to those who appled for more than HK$5 million, it said.
Where one of the pools was undersubscribed, the surplus should be transferred to satisfy demand in the other pool.
The procedures were applicable to all offers which issue their prospectus on or after May 26, 1997, until further notice, it said.
